general_information.Description: I. Course Implementation Orientation Requirements: This course belongs to the specialized knowledge block, taken after students have completed the Japanese language knowledge block and have acquired the core knowledge of Japanese grammar (JIG301) … and supplementary knowledge for the major (Japanese Country and Culture (JSC301), Communication in the Japanese Workplace (JPB301)), … preparing students to accumulate knowledge and meet the requirements for writing the Graduation Thesis/Project. II. Course Objectives: Consolidate and enhance practical language skills through the provision of vocabulary and expressions in the field of literature; Provide basic and foundational knowledge of Japanese literature; help students explore distinctive features, achievements, and the beauty of Japan through literature. Furthermore, by comparing and contrasting similarities and differences with Vietnamese literature, students will gain a deeper understanding of Vietnamese literature, and have reference material to develop projects or theses related to literature; Help students practice self-study skills, searching for relevant materials, synthesizing and presenting them to convey and share information; strengthen teamwork spirit, supporting each other to improve together. (For details, see the LO sheet) III. Course Implementation Format: The course runs for 10 weeks, with 3 slots per week, implemented in the following forms: The instructor delivers integrative, introductory lectures to present key themes and the fundamental contents of Japanese literature, serving as a foundation for students to further study through reading the textbook and expanding knowledge; Students are divided into groups to explore in-depth characteristics of representative genres/forms of Japanese literature (with possible comparisons to Vietnamese literature), choose and analyze representative works corresponding to the genre/form (midterm report) and literary periods (final report), conduct further research, and present findings in class; Select representative works from certain schools of the Modern–Contemporary literary period, divide them into sections for small groups to read together and organize classroom games. The lecture content consists of three parts: (1) Elements of the country, people, culture, writing system, and language that contributed to shaping and creating the distinctive features of Japanese literature; (2) Literary genres/forms of Japanese literature and representative works of these genres/forms; (3) History of Japanese literature (in relation to the historical development of Japan): periods/stages, genres, authors, and representative works of each period. (For details, see the Schedule sheet)
general_information.StudentTasks: Students must attend at least 80% of in-class hours to be eligible for the final exam. Actively participate in discussions and exchanges on topics presented in each lecture. Engage in group work and complete assigned tasks effectively, contributing ideas and information to help the group fulfill its objectives. Prepare lessons and complete assigned exercises seriously and carefully.
general_information.Tools: 1) The instructor summarizes content, checks students’ understanding, provides lecture slides and shared files, and assigns sample exercises for practice. 2) Explore Japanese literature resources through websites suggested in the lecture slides and other relevant online sources related to the course content. 3) Refer to specialized academic materials (see the Materials file).

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Acquire foundational knowledge of Japanese literature, contributing to a deeper understanding of Japan’s cultural identity through literary works

Appreciate the beauty, uniqueness, and artistic value of Japanese literature by analyzing representative works from various genres and historical periods, or by comparing similarities and differences with Vietnamese literature — supporting future research and graduation projects

Strengthen Japanese language proficiency by expanding vocabulary and expressions used in literary contexts, while deepening knowledge of Japanese society and people — enhancing the quality of thesis topics and future professional interactions with Japanese colleagues

Develop research and synthesis skills related to lecture content and assigned topics, learn how to present findings effectively, and inspire others through midterm presentations and final research projects
Cultivate teamwork, lifelong research skills, and a disciplined working style aligned with Japanese professional values

assessments.Question Type: Discussion questions will be provided for each topic raised in class Extended group assignments will be completed and presented as part of the final report
assessments.No Question: 5 to 10 basic questions to reinforce understanding of key concepts 1 to 3 extended questions designed for deeper analysis, aligned with core theoretical foundations of the course and suitable for long-form assignments
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: The depth and complexity of each assignment will be adjusted based on: The volume of information required The level of understanding expected for each topic The progression of lessons throughout the semester
assessments.Grading Guide: Complete all assignments given for each session, actively contribute to lecture development, and participate in class discussions throughout the course.

assessments.Question Type: Evaluation will also consider attendance and participation records
assessments.No Question: Based on the course content, students who attend all sessions will receive a set of questions similar to those outlined in Section 2.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Attendance and participation throughout the semester
assessments.Grading Guide: Attendance and Participation Evaluation The highest score (10 points) is given for full attendance. Absence up to around 20% corresponds to a score of 7 points or above, with intermediate scores calculated based on actual class participation.

assessments.Question Type: Analyze one or more representative authors or literary works from the selected period of Japanese literature
assessments.No Question: Each class session (90 minutes) will feature two student groups presenting on topics related to literary genres and representative works from different historical periods. Each group will present for approximately 30 minutes, followed by 15 minutes of discussion. Presentations should address key questions such as: “Within the same genre, what are the distinctive features of this period?” Discussion questions will vary depending on the characteristics of the genre and the historical context being presented.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Depending on the group’s shared interests, students may choose to explore the same literary genre across different historical periods. The focus should be on: Identifying how the genre’s characteristics evolve over time Highlighting similarities, differences, and new developments in each period Selecting appropriate works and authors for analysis Writing a presentation script and assigning roles to each member for the group report
assessments.Grading Guide: 1) Assess students’ ability to grasp key issues and understand literary genres across different historical periods 2) Evaluate language proficiency, clarity of interpretation, analytical skills, and the ability to select appropriate literary works

assessments.Question Type: Research the assigned topic from the course’s exercise sequence, choose a suitable assignment type for your group, and register for the final presentation
assessments.No Question: Each class session (90 minutes) may also feature two groups presenting on two literary genres and their representative works, with the same structure: 30-minute presentation 15-minute discussion
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Each group may choose different genres, authors, or works and register their topic for presentation. While the format may vary, the core expectations include: Expanding content beyond the textbook and lecture slides Selecting a representative work for the chosen genre Writing a script and assigning individual roles for the presentation
assessments.Grading Guide: Work collaboratively in groups: participate in common activities such as searching for relevant information, synthesizing information, selecting necessary content for reports, writing scripts, and engaging in group activities according to the assignments given by the group leader.
assessments.Note: (Note: For the purpose of presenting midterm and final reports, students may choose to analyze the same genre (in some cases, even the same author/work), but with additional information, viewed from two different perspectives that complement and build upon each other. Therefore, students should be reminded to carefully select and register their topics for these presentations.)

assessments.Question Type: 1) Midterm Contribution (MC): 40% 2) Writing Tasks: 60% total, including: Summary of a literary work: 25% Analysis of a work or excerpt: 35%
assessments.No Question: 1) Theory Test Duration: 30 minutes Weight: 40% Format: 12–15 multiple-choice and true/false questions 2) Essay Writing Duration: 60 minutes Weight: 60% Writing Task 1 (30 minutes): Summarize the content of a literary work Length: 300–500 words Weight: 25% Writing Task 2 (30 minutes): Analyze the beauty and artistic value of a literary work or excerpt Length: 400–500 words Weight: 35%
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: 1) Knowledge of Japanese literary history, genres, and representative authors/works 2) Ability to appreciate and analyze literary works 3) Writing skills and ability to express opinions through clear and effective language
assessments.Grading Guide: 1) Through multiple-choice questions, assess overall knowledge of Japanese literature, understanding of key features, literary streams, and their developmental stages; 2) Through writing tasks, assess the ability to express ideas and the capacity to appreciate literature.
assessments.Note: I. General examination organized by the examination committee\ II. Notes 1. Written assignments may be prepared in advance at home. Students are allowed to choose their preferred authors and works, in order to avoid multiple students working on the same essay (copying or borrowing from one another). They are permitted to revise their work beforehand, and during the test session they are expected to recall and write actively and independently, without cheating; this approach is intended to encourage students’ initiative and active learning. 2. While accurate grammar and writing skills are not the main focus, students must be able to express ideas clearly. Content is prioritized over form. 3. Students may cite previous studies or evaluations, but such references must be integrated into a coherent overall framework. 4. Within the allotted test time, a minimum length is required for the essay, but there is no maximum length. 5. Final exam weighting is as follows5.1 Multiple Choice: 30 minutes – 40% 5.2 Writing: 60 minutes – 60% 5.2.1 Summarizing the content of a literary work (25%) 5.2.2 Analyzing a work or excerpt from a work (35%) III. Course completion requirements Students must meet both of the following conditions: a) Continuous assessment score > 0; Final exam score ≥ 4/10; Overall course score ≥ 5/10. b) In the final exam, no skill may receive a score of 0.
